Ingots with a nominal composition of Fe35Mn15Cr15Ni25Al10 (in at.%) were prepared by arc melting a mixture of metallic elements with a purity greater than 99.9 wt%. An additional 5% of Mn is added to compensate for the evaporation of Mn during melting.
The ingots as-cast were homogenized at 1200 °C for 12 h, and then water quenching.
The alloy plates were subsequently rolled at room temperature to a final thickness of approximately 0.75 mm (from 3 to 0.75 mm)
subjected to annealing at 1200 °C for 10 min.
The annealed specimens were also aged at 700 °C for 1 h, 5 h, 10 h, and 24 h and subsequently cooled in air to room temperature.

Quasi-static tensile tests were performed on dogbone-shaped specimens with gauge dimensions of 13 mm (length) × 3 mm (width) × 0.7 mm (thickness) at a nominal strain rate of 1 × 10-3 s-1 for room temperature (293 K) and liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K).
By prolonging the aging time, the yield strength is strongly enhanced, increasing from 250 MPa to 860 MPa at the peak aging stage.
The mechanical properties of the aged sample A10 have been improved significantly, with a yield strength of 1000 MPa, a tensile strength of 1455 MPa, and a elongation of 9%.
